messages:
Marcus Reed: seeing a small but consistent p99 regression in Hosted canary after turning on profile-pack defaults. Mixed workload route (short prompts + some long contexts) is +6–9% p99 vs control. p50 flat, p95 +1–2%. Anyone else looking at this?

Marcus Reed: graphs (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime-profiles/canary?var=profile_id=h100-default-v1&var=route=chat-completions : p99 token latency and scheduler_queue_ms both up.

Allison Grant: confirmed from dashboards. p99_total_ms and p99_decode_ms both up. also queueing is elevated: scheduler_queue_ms p99 moved from ~18ms -> ~32ms in the canary cohort.

Sofia Ivanova: if queueing moved, it’s likely admission/backpressure + batching. did we change any queue caps w/ the profile defaults?

Lena Fischer: profile pack v1 bumped `batching.max_prefill_tokens_per_batch` and `batching.max_wait_ms` a bit (esp for h100). intent was to improve t/s under load, but could be hurting tail w/ mixed prompt lengths.

Yuki Sato: kernel fallback counters look normal btw. `kernel_choice{attn}=h100_v3` is stable, fallback rate <0.3%. so doesn’t smell like kernel.

Omar El-Sayed: memory headroom/fragmentation looks fine (no new OOM, no compaction spikes). `kv_compaction_ms` is not higher. points back to scheduler/batching.

Sean Gallagher: are we above any rollout SLO gates? (we’re supposed to block if p99 > +5% for 30m on the canary route).

Allison Grant: we’re flirting with it. if you take the last 45m window, p99 is +6.2% normalized. error rates unchanged.

Rafael Mendes: canary is still small cohort. we can pause expansion, but we should decide quickly if we’re changing defaults vs putting in a guardrail.

Marcus Reed: i dug into the request mix. the canary cohort had slightly higher long-context share (not huge). but the delta is present even after normalizing by prompt_len bucket.

Sofia Ivanova: what’s the batch size distribution doing? are we building bigger prefill batches and making short requests wait behind longer prefills?

Lena Fischer: exactly. histogram shows more batches hitting the new prefill token cap. before: prefill batches mostly 4–6 seq. now: 6–10 seq with higher total tokens. queue wait increases because we allow a longer max_wait_ms to “fill”.

Lena Fischer: we also changed `prefill:decode_priority_ratio` to favor prefill slightly more (to keep GPUs fed). in mixed workloads that can starve decode a bit and amplify tail.

Sofia Ivanova: ok, that’s plausible root cause: we improved throughput but introduced extra waiting/variance, esp for decode tail.

Sean Gallagher: can we do a minimal patch: revert the batching wait / prefill cap to previous defaults for H100 profile, and keep the other changes?

Marcus Reed: yes, easiest is revert `max_wait_ms` to 1.0ms (from 2.5ms) for “mixed” bucket and clamp `max_prefill_tokens_per_batch` down a notch.

Sofia Ivanova: but we don’t have “mixed bucket” switching in config-only, right? selection is by workload bucket in scheduler. can we set different knobs per bucket in the profile pack? or is it global today?

Lena Fischer: right now profile is global, but scheduler already tags workload bucket internally (short/medium/long). we can add a small rule: if bucket == mixed/short, lower wait.

Omar El-Sayed: careful on config surface area. but this seems safe.

Allison Grant: for immediate mitigation, we can just revert the global wait and token cap. would likely remove tail regression. then follow-up to make it bucket-aware.

Sofia Ivanova: agree. reduce risk: revert global to previous stable values; we can revisit bucket-aware once perf-canary + gating is in place.

Rafael Mendes: +1. for canary safety: propose
1) stop cohort expansion now
2) ship a hotfix default change
3) re-run canary for 2–4h and compare deltas

Sean Gallagher: can we do it as a profile pack version bump + kill switch? i’d rather not require a full runtime rollback.

Lena Fischer: yep, profile pack supports version pin. we can publish v1.0.1 with safer batching defaults, and set canary to that.

Mateo Alvarez: stepping in — let’s optimize for safety. revert aggressive batching default. throughput gain isn’t worth p99 regression in Hosted.

Mateo Alvarez: action items:
- @Lena Fischer + @Sofia Ivanova: propose the exact knobs to revert + expected impact on t/s
- @Allison Grant: add a quick panel/annotation to show batch wait + avg batch tokens so oncall can see it
- @Rafael Mendes / @Sean Gallagher: pause canary expansion; prep rollback message if needed

Marcus Reed: numbers from benchmark-lab: higher wait gave +3–4% tokens/sec under steady load, but that’s mostly synthetic. real traffic: p50 unchanged, p99 worse. i’m ok trading that back.

Allison Grant: adding the panel is easy. i’ll also add an alert if scheduler_queue_ms p99 jumps >X when profile_version changes.

Yuki Sato: just to close the loop, kernel v3 change is not implicated here. we can keep it.

Sofia Ivanova: agreed on revert.

Lena Fischer: proposed revert for H100 default profile:
- `batching.max_wait_ms`: 2.5 -> 1.0
- `batching.max_prefill_tokens_per_batch`: 8192 -> 6144
- keep `batching.max_decode_tokens_per_batch` as-is (it wasn’t changed)

Lena Fischer: i’ll open a PR for profile pack v1.0.1 and link here.

Sean Gallagher: sounds good. when that lands, SRE will re-enable canary at same cohort size and watch p99 for 2h.

Rafael Mendes: also: please add release note: “revert aggressive batching default due to tail latency in mixed workloads”. easier for oncall.

Marcus Reed: :thumbsup: i’ll comment on the perf-canary thread too so we treat this as a blocking signal for future default changes.

Allison Grant: FYI tagging: canary nodes have `profile_id=h100-default-v1` + `profile_version=1.0.0`. we’ll look for `1.0.1` after deploy.

Mateo Alvarez: thank you. treat this as a good example of why we need the SLO gates + fast rollback. keep the thread updated once v1.0.1 is live.

Lena Fischer: PR up: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/24988 (hotfix) — reverts batching wait + prefill cap in default H100 profile. needs quick review from @Sofia Ivanova + @Marcus Reed.

Sofia Ivanova: reviewed, LGTM. added a TODO for bucket-aware knobs once schema supports it.

Marcus Reed: LGTM. merging once CI passes.

Sean Gallagher: canary expansion paused. once the hotfix is deployed, we’ll run the same cohort + compare p99 over 2h. if p99 delta < +2%, we can proceed.

Allison Grant: also added an annotation rule “profile_version change” to the p99 dashboard so it’s obvious when this flips.

Rafael Mendes: thanks all. please drop a quick note in #incidents if p99 stays elevated after the revert so oncall can track.
